track: TRACK 2 - reproducible spectral structure in residual traces

sec1_periodograms.note: normalized LS power per pass (common.ls_power, irregular time stamps, 200-3000 uHz, 1 uHz grid). Values are per-pass; no cross-frequency pooling is used anywhere.

sec2_candidate_band.null: AR(1) red noise, same irregular time stamps, same n, 1000 surrogates per pass/model

sec2b_null_calibration_and_out_of_sample.purpose: (i) prove the AR(1) surrogate null is correctly calibrated on these irregular time stamps - surrogate realisations fed through the same percentile pipeline must give uniform percentiles; (ii) check the observed band power out-of-sample, since any band chosen by looking at the data is circular.

A.statistic: held-out band power / held-out broad-band power (first half of pass i is not used; second half of pass i+1)

B.statistic: held-out band power / held-out broad-band power (first half of pass i is not used; second half of pass i+1)

C.statistic: held-out band power / held-out broad-band power (first half of pass i is not used; second half of pass i+1)

sec3_comb_test.aggregation: per-pass percentile -> sign test / Wilcoxon across the 22 passes (never across frequencies)
sec3_comb_test.comb_spacing_vs_resolution: comb spacing 50 uHz = 0.237 Rayleigh resolution elements; the whole 860-1310 uHz comb spans 2.13 resolution elements

sec4_reproducibility.note: stacked = unweighted pass-average of the 22 per-pass normalized LS spectra (each pass normalized to its own power scale)

sec4b_stacked_significance.purpose: does the stacked spectrum contain a peak that is unusual relative to (i) an AR(1) red-noise null and (ii) a periodogram-preserving phase-randomised null

phase_randomised_stacked_null.method: circular time shift of each observed pass by a random offset (periodogram-preserving), then the same pass-average and peak-picking as for the real data

sec5_phase_coherence.alignment_assumption: relative_time_min is used as a COMMON time origin across passes. The file provides only relative_time_min, and every pass spans roughly -40..+40 min on its own 1-min grid, so the data are consistent with each pass having its own independent time origin. If the origins are in fact independent, the per-pass fitted phases are independent uniform random variables and the Rayleigh test carries no information (it then has exactly the uniform-phase null reported below). The TESTED ASSUMPTION is therefore: all passes share one absolute time origin, i.e. relative_time_min = t_pass - T0 with the same T0 for all 22 passes.
sec5_phase_coherence.phase_convention: y = A cos(2*pi*f*t - phi), phi = atan2(b, a) from the 2-column LS fit [cos, sin] after linear detrending

A.rayleigh_R_sensitivity_to_pass_time_orig: R is invariant to a COMMON shift of all passes; it changes completely if each pass has its own unknown origin. Equivalent statement: with 22 independent unknown origins the null is exactly the uniform-phase null reported above.

B.rayleigh_R_sensitivity_to_pass_time_orig: R is invariant to a COMMON shift of all passes; it changes completely if each pass has its own unknown origin. Equivalent statement: with 22 independent unknown origins the null is exactly the uniform-phase null reported above.

sec6_spectral_slope.fit: OLS of log10(normalized LS power) on log10(f_uhz), 200-3000 uHz, per pass (frequencies are correlated within a pass; the pass is the unit, only the pass-level slope distribution is reported)

sec7_verdict.statement: NO reproducible localized spectral line at 860-1310 uHz. Median per-pass band percentile A=0.471, B=0.009, C=0.710; passes above the AR(1) 99th percentile A=0/22, B=0/22, C=1/22; stacked peaks at A=489 uHz, B=2474 uHz, C=1706 uHz.
